analysis:
Examined the changed ranges in ClusterSetupWizardLiveOperations.swift (lines ~563-565, 618, 625; units 5-7) and ClusterPublicModels.swift (adds ClusterPublicTensorAssistant, a tensorAssistant field on ClusterPublicModel, a TaskLocal declarationOverride, and tensorAssistant lookup helpers).

Wizard change: the plan step previously computed discoveryMode(mtpMode, coordinator:) up front; now it passes mtpMode and coordinator directly to readAutomatic at lines 616-618 and 623-625. The implementation of readAutomatic and the assistant selection is not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot confirm that coordinator mode still excludes private or undeclared assistants. The fallback calls (lines 630-636) leave coordinator at its default, mode .off, so they should not discover an assistant. The explicit test override at 608-614 (settings.tensorAssistants) is guarded by the mtpMode and kill-switch check and is not coordinator-gated, but it is unchanged and only reachable via test or qualification settings.

PublicModels change: ClusterPublicTensorAssistant.init validates the policy, requires singleton verification, a hash-syntax evidenceSHA256, and a docs/reports/*.md path. tensorAssistant(runtimeModelID:artifactSHA256:) requires the tensorParallel family and a qualifying artifact match through ClusterPairServingGrants, which is sound. The declarationOverride TaskLocal is documented as test-only. It is internal and static, so it is not set by any visible product path, but I could not verify that no product code sets it. The default tensorAssistant is nil, so the behavior change is dormant for every model today. The evidenceSHA256 binding to the report is enforced only by a test, not at runtime.

No concrete regression was found. Remaining integration questions: (1) readAutomatic with coordinator: true must only return the declared public assistant, matching ClusterPublicModels.tensorAssistant. (2) The consumer of resourcePolicyFields in DistributedInstalledNativeStart should change the resource policy hash only when an assistant is declared. (3) The setup-saving and validation path should reject an assistant policy that differs from the declared one.

No threat-model boundary beyond the TB-011 qualification and grant surface is touched. The cache threat T-041 is not affected.
